lines.line: Her cloak had two problems while she sat in her chair.
When the page loaded, the cloak started out as a flat sheet, hanging straight through her lap and the chair.
For about a second it pushed its way out, and then it settled into a shape it never takes again.
Now, before the first frame is drawn, she stands up and sits back down, with the cloth simulated the whole time, so it starts in a natural drape.
After that, the cloak kept trembling slightly. The cloth resting on the seat crept towards the edges, and slipped off a little at a time.
The fix was friction. Cloth resting on the seat now stays where it is, unless something pulls it harder than the seat can hold it.
The cloak no longer jumps when the page loads, and while she sits, it moves a third as much as it used to.
